- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) within 3–5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast by 5–10% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day windows; if forecast is >15% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term downward trend; if sentiment is negative or mixed, apply 5–10% downward adjustment to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1, -1, 1, -1), model tends to misalign with sentiment; adjust forecast to match sentiment direction with 1–3 day lag.
